title: The rehearsal dinner
logline: Thursday. The rehearsal dinner, long tables on the lawn, lanterns. Wood at the far end with a great-aunt who thinks he's the photographer. He lets her. He draws her. She's the best thing he draws all week.

panels.composition: Long tables on the lawn at dusk, lanterns, a hundred people in linen. WOOD at the far end beside a GREAT-AUNT in a cardigan, ninety, delighted with him.

balloons.text: You're the photographer. You've got the hands for it.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, long dinner tables on a lawn at dusk under lanterns with a hundred guests, a thin man in a dark suit at the far end beside a tiny ninety-year-old woman in a cardigan who is delighted with him

panels.composition: Wood, not correcting her. Drawing her instead, under the table's edge.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a thin man drawing surreptitiously beneath a table's edge while an elderly woman beside him talks

panels.composition: The sketchbook: the great-aunt. Twenty lines. The best face of the week — the only face of the week, besides Chloe's, drawn whole.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, close-up of a sketchbook page with a warm precise twenty-line ink portrait of a tiny elderly woman in a cardigan
image.notes: The only full face the arc draws besides Chloe's. Not the groom's, not the guests'. Hers.

panels.composition: Wood tearing the page out and giving it to her. Her face. The lanterns. Far up the table, out of focus, the wedding party.

balloons.text: Oh. Oh, I'm holding still, aren't I.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a thin man handing a torn-out portrait to a delighted elderly woman at a lantern-lit table, the wedding party out of focus far up the table

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: 'Whatever holds still.' The great-aunt: the week's one whole face.
